newsitem.title: CHINA: China punishes Denmark, Netherlands over rights.
newsitem.headline: China punishes Denmark, Netherlands over rights.

text.p: China on Tuesday gave Denmark and the Netherlands a diplomatic slap on the wrist by postponing official visits in a row over their support for a U.N. resolution critical of Beijing's human rights record.

"China ... will delay important exchanges of officials that are under discussion and halt exchanges and cooperation with Denmark on human rights," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing in Beijing.

Beijing then postponed scheduled visits by two Danish ministers. Denmark has been the moving force behing the sponsoring of a resolution in the United Nations Human Rights Commission criticising China's human rights record.
China had warned that relations with countries that co-sponsored the resolution would be affected.
Denmark, the Netherlands, the United States and 12 other countries are co-sponsoring the motion urging China to observe human rights and protect the cultural identity of Tibetans.
The resolution was due to come up for a vote in Geneva later on Tuesday with China on track for a diplomatic triumph as lack of international support left the motion virtually doomed.

Beijing informed Denmark that planned visits to China by Social Affairs Minister Karen Jespersen in June and Justice Minister Frank Jensen in the autumn had been postponed until further notice, the Danish foreign ministry said.
A visit by Danish Education Minister Ole Vig Jensen would go ahead as scheduled in May, as would a private visit by Danish Crown Prince Joachim and Princess Alexandra, set for July.
In The Hague, the Economic Affairs Ministry said China had postponed a Dutch trade mission to Beijing scheduled for June.
The mission would have visited China from June 7 to 14 under leadership of Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers.

"The Netherlands government has learned of this Chinese step with disappointment," the ministry said. "The government of the Netherlands will continue to pursue the further development of political and economic relations with China.
"(Our) relations have until now appeared strong enough to raise even as sensitive a subject as human rights in all openness and through all available channels."
China was expected to try to prevent debate on its human rights record by seeking approval of a pre-emptive "no action" motion it has tabled.
China's Shen did not mention the Netherlands but accused Denmark of interfering in China's internal affairs over its decision to present the resolution.

"Denmark ... is interfering in China's internal affairs and hurting the feelings of the Chinese people," Shen said. Denmark "has set up obstacles to the smooth development of relations between the two countries.
"Sino-Danish relations have been damaged. This is something the Chinese side does not wish to see ... The Chinese side cannot not react," Shen added.
China hoped Denmark would have a change of heart, he said.
"We sincerely hope ... Denmark will change its confrontational method and return to the road of dialogue and cooperation on an equal footing."
China, mainly with support from Asian and African members of the Commission, has fought off European Union and U.S. efforts to have the U.N. body censure Beijing for the past six years in a row.
